\subsection*{Space Complexity --- NSPACE: Results}

\begin{definition}[Deciding a language within a space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b001}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p005-b001}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$
be a language of Boolean strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be a space bound.
The machine decides $L$ within space $s$ if, for every input $x$, there is a time bound
$T$ such that every choice sequence of length $T$ uses at most $s(|x|)$ space, the
machine halts within $T$ steps, and $x\in L$ exactly when the machine accepts within $T$
steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic space complexity class]
\lean{Complexity.NSPACE}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p051-b002}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b002
}
\statementsource{BGW70}{pdf-b9fb35a232af-p005-b001}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace}
For a function $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{NSPACE}(s)$ consists of
the languages of Boolean strings for which there exist a natural number $c$ and a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine that decides the language within space $n\mapsto
c\,s(n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of nondeterministic space]
\lean{Complexity.NSPACE.mono}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s_1,s_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s_1(n)\le s_2(n)$ for every natural
number $n$. Then every language decidable in nondeterministic space bounded by a
constant multiple of $s_1$ is also decidable in nondeterministic space bounded by a
constant multiple of $s_2$; equivalently,
$\mathrm{NSPACE}(s_1)\subseteq\mathrm{NSPACE}(s_2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deterministic space is contained in nondeterministic space]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_subset_NSPACE}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_subset_NSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.FinTM.toFinNDTM_haltsWithin_and_accepts_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the class of binary languages
decidable by finite deterministic Turing machines using space at most a constant
multiple of $s(n)$ is contained in the class decidable by finite nondeterministic Turing
machines under the corresponding space bound.
\end{theorem}
